newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends higher on crude futures gains.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends higher on crude futures gains.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended firmer on moderate gains in crude futures in late trade and amid fairly healthy business, traders said.
Eurograde summer specification barges traded at $216 fob ARA in early trade and there was talk of offers around the $216.50-$217 level, deals at these levels, however, failed to materialise.
In the afternoon, deals were heard at $214 for a barge which could be delivered as either summer or winter specification material, and at $213 and $212.50 fob ARA for wintergrade.
On the swaps front, April swaps traded at $216.50 having wavered around the $215 level for most the day, and were talked around $216.25/$216.75 fob ARA as crude futures picked up.
There were signs that refineries in the region were feeling more optimistic about profit margins.

Texaco Netherlands returned to full capacity in the afternoon at the 400,000 barrel per day Nerefco refinery it shares with British Petroleum. It cut margins by 12.5 percent on March 6 due to poor margins.
Esso Slagen also confirmed it restored runs late last week at its 100,000 bpd refinery in Norway, having cut runs by 15 percent on March 10.
A number of other NWE refineries were also considering the possibility of returning to normal capacity.
Many local players were examining the possibility of sending cargoes trans-Atlantic, especially with the front-end of the NYMEX gasoline futures seemingly pulling the rest of the complex higher.
April NYMEX gasoline was trading 0.49 cent higher at 68.45 cents a gallon, while the May contract was up 0.36 cent at 68.00 cents.
